lean_scaffold:
-- IGProtocol scaffold: VINIT → AFWD → IMSCRIB → CLINK → FSPLIT → EVALT → EVALF → FFUSE → IFIX → TANCH
-- (native ob3ect designer; elaborate against the kernel to verify)
name: the count of four-block six-point configurations in a Steiner

phase_0.boundary_condition: The axioms of a Steiner triple system together with the definition of a Pasch configuration as a four-block six-point subgraph where every point pair appears in exactly one block.
phase_0.domain_name: the count of four-block six-point configurations in a Steiner
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.justification: A forward morphism that takes the given Steiner triple system and produces the set of all 4-block subsets that involve exactly six distinct points.

AREV.justification: Each candidate subgraph is checked against the Pasch incidence relation; this is a reverse traversal that classifies a candidate as matching or not.

CLINK.chosen_element: Sequential composition of enumeration and validation
CLINK.justification: The generation of candidates is chained with the isomorphism check, forming a single pipeline that moves from the STS to a verified verdict on each candidate.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: Contradictory status of the existence check
ENGAGR.justification: In a paraconsistent evaluation the system may simultaneously record a matching subgraph and a proof that none can exist; this token holds that contradiction without attempting to resolve it.

EVALF.justification: On the absence arm exhaustive verification confirms that no candidate matches; constructive falsity (F) is established.

EVALT.justification: On the existence arm at least one candidate subgraph satisfies the definition; constructive truth (T) is established.

FFUSE.chosen_element: Reconciliation of the existence and absence arms
FFUSE.justification: The two investigation arms rejoin into a single state. If the existence arm contributed truth and the absence arm did not, the verdict is T; if absence holds and existence does not, F; if both arms accumulated evidence, the paraconsistent join yields B. The merged state is the final property of the STS.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: Existential branching on Pasch pattern match
FSPLIT.justification: The set of candidates is forked into two arms: one arm where at least one candidate matches the Pasch pattern (existence claim), and the other arm where every candidate fails to match (absence claim).

IFIX.chosen_element: Permanent ledger entry for the count verdict
IFIX.justification: The resolved property (T, F, or B) is appended to the proof corpus as an immutable lemma about the given Steiner triple system.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: Self-consistent incidence of the Steiner triple system
IMSCRIB.justification: The system references its own block-point memberships without altering them; it is simply the recognition that the structure is what it is.

TANCH.chosen_element: Sealed verdict on the presence of a Pasch configuration
TANCH.justification: The terminal anchor permanently closes the evaluation; after this point the answer (contains / does not contain / both) is fixed and no further transformation can alter it.

VINIT.justification: Before any vertices or triples are introduced, the system is a void without a specific STS; no property can be asserted.

phase_2.fuse_result: A single resolved state: T if constructive truth was contributed, F if constructive falsity was contributed, B if both arms contributed evidence, N if neither arm established anything (which does not occur when the input is a valid STS).
phase_2.rejoin_note: Arm T carries the work of attempting to locate a matching subgraph; arm F carries the exhaustive proof that none exists. The arms rejoin into a single assertion about the presence of a Pasch configuration. The kernel computes the B4 value over SIXTEEN_3 from the evidence gathered on the arms.
phase_2.split_input: The set of all 4-block 6-point subgraphs extracted from the Steiner triple system
split_outputs: Arm T: at least one subgraph satisfies the Pasch incidence relation
Arm F: exhaustive verification finds no subgraph that satisfies the relation
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B — the system simultaneously affirms and denies the existence of a Pasch configuration, a live contradiction that is not resolved.
phase_3.false_description: F — the Steiner triple system contains no such configuration; it is Pasch‑free.
phase_3.true_description: T — the Steiner triple system contains at least one four-block six-point Pasch configuration.
phase_3.void_description: N — the system is uninitalized; no Steiner triple system has been fixed nor any candidate considered.

steps.domain_action: The candidate Steiner triple system enters as an uninitialized incidence structure.
Enumerate all 4‑block subsets of the system that involve exactly six distinct points.
Verify that the selected blocks respect the system’s own incidence — a self‑reference that needs no external criterion.
Chain the enumeration with per‑candidate pattern validation, composing the subgraph generation and the checking step.
Fork the candidate set into two arms: one where at least one candidate matches the Pasch pattern, the other where none match.
Arm T — a matching Pasch subgraph is identified; constructive truth (existence) is recorded.
Arm F — exhaustive checking confirms every candidate fails; constructive falsity (absence) is recorded.
The arms rejoin into a single verdict, fusing the evidence using Belnap join. Conflicting evidence yields B.
The resulting property (T/F/B) is fixed permanently as a lemma about the structure.
The evaluation is sealed; no further modification can alter the determination of whether the Steiner triple system harbours a Pasch configuration.

phase_5.alfs_store: The canonical Lean file that defines `SteinerTripleSystem`, `PaschConfig`, and the counting lemma, serving as the bootstrap reference for the object.
phase_5.compiler_frontend: The formalisation layer that translates the combinatorial definition of a Steiner triple system and a Pasch configuration into kernel‑executable operations.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Message passing between the subgraph enumerator and the pattern checker, carrying candidates and their verification flags.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: A register file that stores the current candidate, a cumulative flag indicating whether a match has been found, and the final verdict.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: A simple loop that iterates over each 4‑block subset, dispatching it to the checking routine, and aggregates the outcome.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The enumeration of 4‑block subsets scales as O(v^3) in the number v of points; each candidate requires an O(1) isomorphism check.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the verdict was already latent in the incidence structure; the process merely extracts it without increasing the system’s information-theoretic entropy.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A Steiner triple system whose verdict (contains / does not contain / both) has been determined and recorded.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A Steiner triple system whose Pasch status is unknown.
